questions.stem: In simple terms, what is a Data Pipeline?
options: A set of rules for classifying data
The travelling of data from one point to another
A database backup mechanism
A tool for masking sensitive data
A dashboard for monitoring servers
questions.explanation: A Data Pipeline is as simple as data travelling from one point to another, yet without a reliable one no decision can be taken on time.

questions.stem: In the Pull data processing mechanism, which system initiates the movement of data?
options: The source system pushes data to the target
A third-party broker moves the data
Data flows continuously with no initiator
The target system pulls data from the source system
The BI tool requests data from the warehouse
questions.explanation: Pull is when target systems pull data from source systems; Push is when source systems push data to targets.

questions.stem: By what other name is Bulk Loading known?
options: Data Dump
Data Stream
Data Delta
Data Snapshot
Data Trickle
questions.explanation: Bulk Loading, processing the whole set of data every time from the source, is also called a Data Dump.

options: The whole dataset every time
Only the metadata of the source
Only the data that has changed at the source
A random sample of the source
Only deleted records
questions.explanation: CDC Loading means processing only the changed data from the source, unlike Bulk Loading which processes everything.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of Batch processing in a Data Pipeline?
options: Moving a post the moment it is liked
Streaming CCTV footage second by second
Pushing a card transaction instantly
Sending an OTP on payment
Starting processing after 24 hours or perhaps 12 hours
questions.explanation: Batch processing means processing data after a certain time duration, for example after 24 or 12 hours.

questions.stem: Which example illustrates Real-Time (event-based) processing in a Data Pipeline?
options: A nightly load of the sales table
A post being LIKED on Facebook or LinkedIn moving immediately to downstream systems
A weekly data dump to the warehouse
A monthly financial close
A quarterly data archive
questions.explanation: Real-Time processing means the moment there is a change in the source, that piece of data is processed towards the target, such as a LIKE on Facebook or LinkedIn.

questions.stem: What effect does better hardware have on Batch processing?
options: It removes the need for a data pipeline
It makes bulk loading impossible
It converts batch into streaming automatically
It allows the batch time duration to be made smaller
It has no effect on batch duration
questions.explanation: The better the hardware in place, the smaller the batch processing time duration can be.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the named Data Processing Mechanisms?
options: Push
Pull
Merge
Streaming
None of these; all are named mechanisms
questions.explanation: The Data Processing Mechanisms are Push, Pull and Streaming; Merge is not one of them.

questions.stem: What is the likely future for an organisation that builds Data Pipelines without Data Lineage, a Data Catalog and Data Governance standards?
options: A Data Swamp
A Data Vault
A Data Mart
Faster decision making
Lower hardware costs
questions.explanation: When creating Data Pipelines one must ensure Lineage, Catalog and Governance standards and policies are in place, or a Data Swamp is the future.

questions.stem: Why does CDC play a vital role in supporting Real-Time processing from OLTP systems?
options: Because OLTP systems cannot be queried directly
Because CDC converts data into batches
Because CDC encrypts data before transfer
Because CDC replaces the need for a data warehouse
Because in real time a very small size of data is expected to travel
questions.explanation: To support real-time from OLTP, CDC plays a vital role because in real time only a very small amount of data is expected to travel.
